      "unit": "F021",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "For the purposes of providing blind persons with remunerative employment, enlarging the economic opportunities of the blind, and stimulating the blind to greater efforts in striving to make themselves self-supporting, blind persons licensed under the provisions of 20 U.S.C. ch. 6A shall be authorized to operate vending facilities on any Federal property.",

    {
      "unit": "F023",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "In authorizing the operation of vending facilities on Federal property, priority shall be given to blind persons licensed by a State agency as provided in this chapter.",

        "actor_quote": null,
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",

      "unit": "F023:F025",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "In authorizing the operation of vending facilities on Federal property, the Secretary, through the Commissioner, shall, after consultation with the Administrator of General Services and other heads of departments, agencies, or instrumentalities of the United States in control of the maintenance, operation, and protection of Federal property, prescribe regulations designed to assure that (1) priority under subsection (b) is given to such licensed blind persons (including assignment of vending machine income pursuant to section 107d–3 of this title to achieve and protect such priority), and (2) wherever feasible, one or more vending facilities are established on all Federal property to the extent that any such facility or facilities would not adversely affect the interests of the United States.",

        "actor_quote": "the Secretary, through the Commissioner",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": "In authorizing the operation of vending facilities on Federal property, after consultation with the Administrator of General Services and other heads of departments, agencies, or instrumentalities of the United States in control of the maintenance, operation, and protection of Federal property",

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Any limitation on the placement or operation of a vending facility based on a finding that such placement or operation would adversely affect the interests of the United States shall be fully justified in writing to the Secretary, who shall determine whether such limitation is justified.",
        "actor": null,
        "actor_quote": null,

        "scope_text": "Any limitation on the placement or operation of a vending facility based on a finding that such placement or operation would adversely affect the interests of the United States",

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "The Commissioner shall, within one hundred and eighty days after enactment of the Randolph-Sheppard Act Amendments of 1974, establish requirements for the uniform application of this chapter by each State agency designated under paragraph (5) of 20 U.S.C. 107a(a), including appropriate accounting procedures, policies on the selection and establishment of new vending facilities, distribution of income to blind vendors, and the use and control of set-aside funds under section 107b(3) of this title.",

      "unit_attributes": {

        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "The Secretary of Education shall designate as provided in section 107b of this title the State agency for the blind in each State, or, in any State in which there is no such agency, some other public agency to issue licenses to blind persons who are citizens of the United States for the operating of vending facilities on Federal and other property in such State for the vending of newspapers, periodicals, confections, tobacco products, foods, beverages, and other articles or services dispensed automatically or manually and prepared on or off the premises in accordance with all applicable health laws, as determined by the State licensing agency, and including the vending or exchange of chances for any lottery authorized by State law and conducted by an agency of a State.",

      "unit": "F080",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": [
          "satisfactory_site"
        ],
        "statement": "After January 1, 1975, no department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States shall undertake to acquire by ownership, rent, lease, or to otherwise occupy, in whole or in part, any building unless, after consultation with the head of such department, agency, or instrumentality and the State licensing agency, it is determined by the Secretary that (A) such building includes a satisfactory site or sites for the location and operation of a vending facility by a blind person, or (B) if a building is to be constructed, substantially altered, or renovated, or in the case of a building that is already occupied on such date by such department, agency, or instrumentality, is to be substantially altered or renovated for use by such department, agency, or instrumentality, the design for such construction, substantial alteration, or renovation includes a satisfactory site or sites for the location and operation of a vending facility by a blind person.",

        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": [

        ],
        "statement": "Each department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States shall provide notice to the appropriate State licensing agency of its plans for occupation, acquisition, renovation, or relocation of a building adequate to permit such State agency to determine whether such building includes a satisfactory site or sites for a vending facility.",
        "actor": "Each such department, agency, or instrumentality",

        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": null,

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "The provisions of 20 U.S.C. 107a(d)(1) shall not apply when the Secretary and the State licensing agency determine that the number of people using the property is or will be insufficient to support a vending facility.",
        "actor": null,
        "actor_quote": null,

      "unit_attributes": {

        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "The provisions of 20 U.S.C. 107a(d)(1) shall not apply to any privately owned building, any part of which is leased by any department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States and in which, (i) prior to the execution of such lease, the lessor or any of his tenants had in operation a restaurant or other food facility in a part of the building not included in such lease, and (ii) the operation of such a vending facility by a blind person would be in proximate and substantial direct competition with such restaurant or other food facility.",

unit_attributes.statement: For the purposes of providing blind persons with remunerative employment, enlarging the economic opportunities of the blind, and stimulating the blind to greater efforts in striving to make themselves self-supporting, blind persons licensed under the provisions of 20 U.S.C. ch. 6A shall be authorized to operate vending facilities on any Federal property.
In authorizing the operation of vending facilities on Federal property, priority shall be given to blind persons licensed by a State agency as provided in this chapter.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In authorizing the operation of vending facilities on Federal property

unit_attributes.statement: In authorizing the operation of vending facilities on Federal property, the Secretary, through the Commissioner, shall, after consultation with the Administrator of General Services and other heads of departments, agencies, or instrumentalities of the United States in control of the maintenance, operation, and protection of Federal property, prescribe regulations designed to assure that (1) priority under subsection (b) is given to such licensed blind persons (including assignment of vending machine income pursuant to section 107d–3 of this title to achieve and protect such priority), and (2) wherever feasible, one or more vending facilities are established on all Federal property to the extent that any such facility or facilities would not adversely affect the interests of the United States.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In authorizing the operation of vending facilities on Federal property, after consultation with the Administrator of General Services and other heads of departments, agencies, or instrumentalities of the United States in control of the maintenance, operation, and protection of Federal property

unit_attributes.statement: Any limitation on the placement or operation of a vending facility based on a finding that such placement or operation would adversely affect the interests of the United States shall be fully justified in writing to the Secretary, who shall determine whether such limitation is justified.
unit_attributes.scope_text: Any limitation on the placement or operation of a vending facility based on a finding that such placement or operation would adversely affect the interests of the United States

unit_attributes.statement: A determination made by the Secretary pursuant to the provision governing limitation on the placement or operation of a vending facility shall be binding on any department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States affected by such determination.
The Secretary shall publish the determination on whether a limitation on the placement or operation of a vending facility is justified, along with supporting documentation, in the Federal Register.
The Secretary of Education shall insure that the Rehabilitation Services Administration is the principal agency for carrying out this chapter.

The Commissioner shall, within one hundred and eighty days after enactment of the Randolph-Sheppard Act Amendments of 1974, establish requirements for the uniform application of this chapter by each State agency designated under paragraph (5) of 20 U.S.C. 107a(a), including appropriate accounting procedures, policies on the selection and establishment of new vending facilities, distribution of income to blind vendors, and the use and control of set-aside funds under section 107b(3) of this title.
unit_attributes.scope_text: within one hundred and eighty days after enactment of the Randolph-Sheppard Act Amendments of 1974

unit_attributes.statement: The Secretary of Education shall, through the Commissioner, make annual surveys of concession vending opportunities for blind persons on Federal and other property in the United States, particularly with respect to Federal property under the control of the General Services Administration, the Department of Defense, and the United States Postal Service.
The Secretary of Education shall make surveys throughout the United States of industries with a view to obtaining information that will assist blind persons to obtain employment.

The Secretary of Education shall make available to the public, and especially to persons and organizations engaged in work for the blind, information obtained as a result of surveys under 20 U.S.C. 107a(a).

The Secretary of Education shall designate as provided in section 107b of this title the State agency for the blind in each State, or, in any State in which there is no such agency, some other public agency to issue licenses to blind persons who are citizens of the United States for the operating of vending facilities on Federal and other property in such State for the vending of newspapers, periodicals, confections, tobacco products, foods, beverages, and other articles or services dispensed automatically or manually and prepared on or off the premises in accordance with all applicable health laws, as determined by the State licensing agency, and including the vending or exchange of chances for any lottery authorized by State law and conducted by an agency of a State.

The Secretary of Education shall, through the Commissioner, conduct periodic evaluations of the program authorized by this chapter, including upward mobility and other training required by section 107d–4 of this title.

The Secretary of Education shall, through the Commissioner, take such other steps, including the issuance of such rules and regulations, as may be necessary or desirable in carrying out the provisions of this chapter.
The State licensing agency shall, in issuing each license for the operation of a vending facility, give preference to blind persons who are in need of employment.
unit_attributes.scope_text: in issuing each such license for the operation of a vending facility

unit_attributes.statement: Each license for the operation of a vending facility shall be issued for an indefinite period but may be terminated by the State licensing agency if it is satisfied that the facility is not being operated in accordance with the rules and regulations prescribed by such licensing agency.

The State licensing agency may terminate a vending facility license if it is satisfied that the facility is not being operated in accordance with the rules and regulations prescribed by such licensing agency.
unit_attributes.scope_text: if it is satisfied that the facility is not being operated in accordance with the rules and regulations prescribed by such licensing agency

unit_attributes.statement: Licenses for the operation of a vending facility shall be issued only to applicants who are blind within the meaning of section 107e of this title.

The State licensing agency designated by the Secretary is authorized, with the approval of the head of the department or agency in control of the maintenance, operation, and protection of the Federal property on which the facility is to be located but subject to regulations prescribed pursuant to section 107 of this title, to select a location for such facility and the type of facility to be provided.
unit_attributes.actor: The State licensing agency designated by the Secretary
unit_attributes.actor_quote: The State licensing agency designated by the Secretary
unit_attributes.scope_text: with the approval of the head of the department or agency in control of the maintenance, operation, and protection of the Federal property on which the facility is to be located but subject to regulations prescribed pursuant to section 107 of this title

unit_attributes.statement: After January 1, 1975, no department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States shall undertake to acquire by ownership, rent, lease, or to otherwise occupy, in whole or in part, any building unless, after consultation with the head of such department, agency, or instrumentality and the State licensing agency, it is determined by the Secretary that (A) such building includes a satisfactory site or sites for the location and operation of a vending facility by a blind person, or (B) if a building is to be constructed, substantially altered, or renovated, or in the case of a building that is already occupied on such date by such department, agency, or instrumentality, is to be substantially altered or renovated for use by such department, agency, or instrumentality, the design for such construction, substantial alteration, or renovation includes a satisfactory site or sites for the location and operation of a vending facility by a blind person.
unit_attributes.actor: department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States
unit_attributes.actor_quote: department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States

unit_attributes.statement: Each department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States shall provide notice to the appropriate State licensing agency of its plans for occupation, acquisition, renovation, or relocation of a building adequate to permit such State agency to determine whether such building includes a satisfactory site or sites for a vending facility.
unit_attributes.actor: Each such department, agency, or instrumentality
unit_attributes.actor_quote: Each such department, agency, or instrumentality

unit_attributes.statement: The provisions of 20 U.S.C. 107a(d)(1) shall not apply when the Secretary and the State licensing agency determine that the number of people using the property is or will be insufficient to support a vending facility.
unit_attributes.scope_text: when the Secretary and the State licensing agency determine that the number of people using the property is or will be insufficient to support a vending facility

unit_attributes.statement: The provisions of 20 U.S.C. 107a(d)(1) shall not apply to any privately owned building, any part of which is leased by any department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States and in which, (i) prior to the execution of such lease, the lessor or any of his tenants had in operation a restaurant or other food facility in a part of the building not included in such lease, and (ii) the operation of such a vending facility by a blind person would be in proximate and substantial direct competition with such restaurant or other food facility.
unit_attributes.scope_text: to any privately owned building, any part of which is leased by any department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States and in which, (i) prior to the execution of such lease, the lessor or any of his tenants had in operation a restaurant or other food facility in a part of the building not included in such lease, and (ii) the operation of such a vending facility by a blind person would be in proximate and substantial direct competition with such restaurant or other food facility

unit_attributes.statement: Each department, agency, and instrumentality shall make every effort to lease property in privately owned buildings capable of accommodating a vending facility.

unit_attributes.statement: For the purposes of 20 U.S.C. 107a(d), the term “satisfactory site” means an area determined by the Secretary to have sufficient space, electrical and plumbing outlets, and such other facilities as the Secretary may by regulation prescribe, for the location and operation of a vending facility by a blind person.
unit_attributes.scope_text: For the purposes of this subsection

unit_attributes.statement: In any State having an approved plan for vocational rehabilitation pursuant to the Vocational Rehabilitation Act or the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the State licensing agency designated under paragraph (5) of subsection (a) of 20 U.S.C. 107a shall be the State agency designated under section 101(a)(2)(A) of such Rehabilitation Act of 1973.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In any State having an approved plan for vocational rehabilitation pursuant to the Vocational Rehabilitation Act or the Rehabilitation Act of 1973
